dc_herald.text: Henry II built this Great Tower in the 1180s, partly to impress the pilgrims landing at Dover on their way to Becket's tomb. It worked. It still does.
The walls are up to six metres thick. In 1216 French invaders under Prince Louis besieged the castle for months and undermined the north gate. It held. Just.

dc_cook.text: We've set the hall as it was for a royal visit: bright painted walls, hangings, gold plate. Medieval people didn't live in grey stone if they could help it.
